item.description:
Health officials report 753 fresh cases of dengue inflection, 3 deaths overnight
Health officials on Tuesday said they recorded 753 fresh cases of dengue, with at least three people dying from the disease in the past 24 hours.
“During the period, 98 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division, 94 in Chittagong division, 51 in Dhaka division, 106 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) areas and 135 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 135 in Khulna division, 61 in Mymensingh division, 46 in Rajshahi division, 24 in Rangpur division and three in Sylhet division,” a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the beginning of the dengue outbreak this year, Bangladesh has recorded 74 deaths and 25,601 cases.
Last year, dengue claimed 413 lives and infected 102,861 people in the country. In 2024, the disease claimed 575 lives and infected 101,214 people.

item.title: Is Bangladesh facing a resurgence of militancy?
item.description:
There were fears of a resurgence of militancy after several terrorists escaped from jail during the mass uprising two years ago. Some militants were also released following the fall of the Awami League government.
Whether those fears are now going to become a reality is the subject of discussion.
There was a hint that the situation could turn chaotic in early July, when flags bearing Arabic letters were suddenly seen flying in various parts of the country. The main cause for concern was the association of this flag with international terrorism.
As concerns over the flags began to subside, a major incident emerged as “evidence” of the resurgence of militancy.
On the 12th of this month, police conducted a raid in Savar, near Dhaka, and recovered several bombs and bomb-making equipment.
One large bomb was defused the following day.
What is particularly worrying is that those arrested by police and charged under the Anti-Terrorism Act have been identified as members of neo-JMB (Jamaatul Mujahideen Bangladesh).
Al-Qaeda’s shadow
Nazmul Hasan alias “Bomaru” Mamun, whom police are looking for in connection with the Savar incident and other blasts, was arrested nine years ago. However, in January this year, a court acquitted him in a 2017 blast case.
The verdict also described Mamun as an “anti-fascist activist,” according to media reports.
Meanwhile, a UN Security Council report warned that Al-Qaeda’s Indian subcontinent branch, Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent or AQIS, has increased its activities in Bangladesh and is trying to build a network in Bangladesh through active cells.
Two days after the report was published, a neo-JMB cell was uncovered in Savar and weapons were recovered.
There has always been controversy over the presence of militancy in Bangladesh and its international connections, particularly during the Awami League’s rule from 2009 to 2024.
In an attempt to discredit the anti-militancy operations of the police and RAB, some quarters alleged that although the government claimed to be combating terrorism, its main objective was to suppress the opposition.
Even the killings of bloggers that began in 2013 were suspected to have been the work of militants.
History of Holey Artisan
On the other hand, the Awami League government was intent on describing militant activities solely as “domestic terrorism.”
At various times, it denied the international connections of domestic militants, particularly their links to Al-Qaeda and the Islamic State. But after the terrorist attack on the Holey Artisan Bakery in Gulshan, Dhaka, on July 1, 2016, which killed 24 people, including two senior police officers, the foreign involvement became clear.
The Islamic State’s news agency, Amaq, was the first to publish on social media a photograph of a bloodied body lying on the floor inside the O Kitchen restaurant adjacent to the Holey Artisan Bakery.
After the five terrorists were killed in the army operation, Amaq was also the first to publish photographs of them smiling with weapons in their hands and keffiyehs on their heads.
It is understood that the terrorists had sent their photographs before embarking on the operation.
The government, probably fearing involvement in the US-led “war on terror,” tried to portray the country’s militant activities as “domestic.”
After the Holey Artisan attack, the police and RAB carried out extensive operations in various parts of the country, killing and arresting suspected militants.
As a result of these operations, there were no major attacks in the country after the Holey Artisan incident.
However, the police and RAB did not receive much praise for this, mainly because of allegations that the anti-militancy campaign was being used to “suppress dissent.”
After the mass uprising two years ago, the words “militant drama” were seen written on various walls. In other words, an attempt was made to dismiss the anti-terror operations as mere drama.
The sculpture erected in front of Gulshan Police Station in memory of the two officers killed in the Holey Artisan attack was demolished and has not been rebuilt to this day.
Even the name of martyred AC Rabiul Karim has been removed from the gate of the Detective Branch office in Dhaka.
A ceremony was held at the Italian Embassy to mark the tenth anniversary of the attack, as many of the victims were Italian citizens, but no memorial service was held by the Bangladesh government or even the police authorities.
Looking at the course of events, it appears that the post-2024 ruling establishment is not only trying to downplay the significance of the most tragic terrorist attack in Bangladesh’s history, but is also trying to erase the memory of the police officers killed in the attack.
‘Bangla Bhai’ and ‘Shaykh Abdur Rahman’
As Islamist parties played a significant role in the fall of the Awami League government, various extremist groups moved to the centre of politics.
Using this newfound power, they tried to erase the militant activities of past years from the criminal record, as evidenced by the aftermath of the Holey Artisan incident.
At the same time, they portrayed the Awami League government’s anti-terrorism activities as the suppression of opposition views.
Dr Muhammad Yunus’s interim government sought to legitimize this new narrative through its silence.
It is important to remember here that what is understood as “terrorism” in today’s world began to emerge in Bangladesh during another period of BNP rule.
During the BNP-Jamaat alliance government from 2001 to 2006, the activities of JMB began to come to light.
The extremist leader known as “Bangla Bhai” established a reign of terror in the northern region. Another militant leader, Shaykh Abdur Rahman, also gained notoriety.
After coming to power, the BNP government does not appear to be prioritizing the suppression of militant activities. There is no emphasis on apprehending the militants who escaped from jail in 2024, nor is there any process to take back into custody militant leaders who were released by the courts.
Taken together, the Savar incident and the Security Council’s warning make it difficult for the government to maintain the “militant drama” narrative.
More than that, ignoring the possibility of a resurgence of militancy could put the country’s security at risk.
Tough decision before the government
The Yunus government’s compromising policy towards extremists led to the demolition of the “Bangabandhu Memorial Museum” at Dhanmondi 32, where Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was assassinated on August 15, 1975.
Because the Yunus government had indulged the extremists, they also vandalized and set fire to the offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star, remaining beyond the reach of the authorities.
The public was made to believe, through various means, that followers of Islamic politics had been forced to choose the path of terrorism because they had been persecuted for so long.
The propaganda suggested that if they were allowed to enter mainstream politics, they would return to systematic, democratic, and peaceful activities.
But for those whose ideology is rooted in extreme extremism, where there is no room for dissent and no value placed on tolerance, the objective -- regardless of the political trend -- will be to establish absolute dominance over society.
The question now is whether the government will acknowledge that there is indeed a threat of a resurgence of militancy in the country and that some tough steps need to be taken to prevent it.
Sabir Mustafa is former head of BBC Bangla and is currently working as a freelance journalist and podcaster. Views expressed are the writer’s own.

Muhit: Advanced eye care to be available at upazila level
item.description:
State Minister for Health and Family Welfare Dr MA Muhit has said advanced eye care will be made available at the upazila level, with separate outdoor, indoor and operation theatre facilities for eye treatment to be introduced at the 151-bed full-fledged hospitals currently under construction in every upazila.
“At the same time, the government is finalising an integrated National Eye Care Plan with targets of conducting around 10 lakh cataract surgeries, distributing several crore pairs of spectacles and providing treatment for diabetic retinopathy across the country,” he said.
The state minister made the remarks while formally inaugurating the World Health Organization’s "WHO SPECS 2030 Initiative" at a hotel in the capital on Tuesday.
Dr Muhit said the government is giving the highest priority to the health sector and is committed to taking modern eye care services to the upazila level. The work of transforming upazila health complexes into 151-bed full-fledged hospitals is underway.
“Advanced eye care facilities will be provided in around 500 upazilas so that people at the grassroots no longer have to travel to district towns or the capital for treatment,” he said.
Highlighting the government’s plan to strengthen primary healthcare at the grassroots, the health state minister further said primary eye care would be included as a mandatory component in the training of one lakh health workers currently being recruited by the government.
Referring to plans to increase the capacity of the National Institute of Ophthalmology and Hospital (NIOH), the state minister said a major project has been undertaken to modernize and expand the institute, which will be implemented soon.
Over the past six months, the Ministry of Health has been regularly coordinating with international and local organizations to improve and expand eye care services. Through high-level government efforts, Bangladesh has also secured a major commitment to host a global summit, he said.
Acting Director of the National Institute of Ophthalmology and Hospital Professor Dr ASMM Qaudir, WHO Regional Adviser Dr Tashi Tobgay and WHO Representative to Bangladesh Dr Ahmed Jamsheed Mohammed, among others, spoke at the program.

item.title: Fisheries sector eyes export growth after meeting domestic demand
item.description:
Bangladesh has achieved self-sufficiency in meeting its domestic fish demand, and is now focusing on expanding fisheries exports, State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock Sultan Salauddin Tuku said Tuesday.
“The fisheries sector has achieved full self-sufficiency in meeting domestic demand. Now our priority is to increase exports,” the state minister said, in remarks addressing a discussion as part of National Fisheries Fortnight 2026, organised by the Department of Fisheries at its conference room.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday formally inaugurated the National Fisheries Fortnight-2026 at a programme held in Kotiadi in Kishoreganj, aiming to further strengthen the fisheries sector to advance the government's goal of building a self-reliant and welfare-oriented Bangladesh.
Explaining the decision to hold the central event outside the capital in Kishoreganj, Tuku said haor areas play a vital role in the country's freshwater fish production.
“Haors account for a major portion of our freshwater fish supply. Holding the event outside Dhaka enabled us to connect directly with marginal fish farmers, fishermen and local stakeholders,” he said.
The state minister said former President Ziaur Rahman initiated key programmes, including river dredging and canal excavation, while former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia expanded development initiatives in the sector.
He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is continuing support for agriculture and fisheries and has approved new sector-specific projects aimed at strengthening the rural economy.
Tuku also urged public servants to perform their duties with transparency, sincerity and dedication.
“Power belongs to the people. Public servants must fulfil their responsibilities without negligence and work transparently for public welfare,” he said.
Fisheries and Livestock Secretary Delwar Hossain, speaking as a special guest, instructed officials to ensure hassle-free delivery of government services.
“Fish farmers and citizens must not face harassment while seeking government services. Any negligence in official duties will be met with strict accountability,” he warned.
Chairing the programme, Department of Fisheries Director General Khaled Kanak said the central event of National Fisheries Fortnight was last held outside Dhaka in 2003.
He said holding this year's main event in Katiadi, Kishoreganj, and recognising field-level farmers had generated renewed enthusiasm among stakeholders in the fisheries sector.
Senior officials of the ministry and Department of Fisheries, sector representatives and local fish farmers attended the closing ceremony.

item.title: West Bank siege exposes Israel army inaction on settler violence
item.description:
The Israeli military is touted as the most powerful in the Middle East, striking targets deep into enemy territory. But for more than a week, Israeli troops have somehow failed to evict a small group of settlers sitting on rocks in the occupied West Bank.
Experts says the military has long shown inertia when its task is stopping surging violence against Palestinians, due to government backing for the settlement movement and the increasing influence of settler ideology within the army’s ranks.
More than a week ago, a handful of settlers at Qusra near Nablus began besieging Palestinians inside their homes, blocking supplies and drawing international and even domestic condemnation.
The Israeli military repeatedly deployed troops, with the United States saying it had requested action by its ally as one of the besieged Palestinians is a US citizen.
But beyond condemnatory statements, the detention of one Israeli, and the dismantling of settlers’ tents, little was done to force them out.
Some of the first soldiers to arrive at the scene were even filmed praying with the settlers. The military later vowed disciplinary action.
By Monday, settlers on quadbikes were back at the site shaking hands and chatting with Israeli forces, according to videos shared with AFP by a besieged resident.
The government’s support for extremist settlers puts the military in an “impossible situation,” said Nimrod Novik, a senior advisor and special envoy to former Israeli prime minister Shimon Peres.
The military is “forced to choose between operating on the basis of its professional judgement and duty, which calls for applying harsh measures against violent settlers, or... adhere to government policy, which provides those terrorists with political backwind as well as resources,” he told AFP.
“The result is paralysis with rare exceptions due either to the severity of the crimes or US intervention,” Novik added.
Israel has since 1967 occupied the West Bank, where more than 500,000 Israelis now live in settlements which are illegal under international law. The territory is home to some three million Palestinians.
Construction of settlements has reached historic highs under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing government, with several ministers cheering the establishment of outposts deemed illegal even under Israeli law and openly calling for the territory’s annexation.
Settler violence against Palestinians has persisted for years, with perpetrators in most cases facing no repercussions, but recent months have seen a dramatic surge in attacks.
“The infrastructure of the occupation is built in a way that for a soldier, for us, it’s almost impossible to enforce the law on violent settlers and very easy to do whatever we want on Palestinians,” said Nadav Weiman, a former sniper who now heads Breaking the Silence, an advocacy group for Israeli veterans.
Weiman told AFP that the rules of engagement for dealing with settlers were rarely explained, with soldiers told to refer to police due to their status as Israeli citizens.
“In 22 years of collecting testimonies from soldiers in the West Bank, I can tell you that in the majority of the units, nothing is being told to the soldier on what they can do with settlers,” he added.
The reluctance to act also comes from increasingly blurred lines between settlers and soldiers in the West Bank, Weiman said, with a growing number of settlers becoming officers after attending hardline ideological pre-military academies.
The military’s commander for the West Bank, Major General Avi Bluth, himself attended the Bnei David pre-military academy in the settlement of Eli.
A further blurring happened following Hamas’s October 7, 2023 resistance campaign against Israel.
With most soldiers sent to fight in Gaza or Lebanon, the military drafted thousands of settler reservists into regional defense units, tasked with securing their own communities in the West Bank.
According to rights group Yesh Din, around 7,000 settlers were armed and mobilized into these units during the first months of the war, with such reservists more likely to do nothing to stop settler attacks or to participate themselves.
While many are no longer on active reserve duty, the military has allowed them to keep their firearms and uniforms, according to Yesh Din, enabling soaring violence by settlers posing as soldiers.
When contacted by AFP, the military said the main body responsible for handling violations by Israeli citizens in the West Bank is the police, with soldiers instructed to “act to stop the violation and to delay or detain the suspects until the police arrive at the scene.”
“In situations where soldiers fail to adhere to IDF orders, the incidents are thoroughly reviewed, and disciplinary actions are implemented accordingly,” it added.
In the wake of the Qusra siege, Israel’s Defense Minister Israel Katz has called for the police to take over West Bank law enforcement, saying it is not soldiers’ responsibility to “chase” violent settlers.
The measure, while unlikely to be implemented soon, would be a step towards Israeli annexation of the territory.
Observers doubt the political will to crack down on violent settlers ahead of October 27 elections, but say the issue should be treated with urgency.
“Should settler violence continue, it will be astonishing if a major bloody conflagration doesn’t ensue,” Novik said.

item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal has taken cognisance of formal charges against 38 people, including former Rajshahi City Corporation mayor AHM Khairuzzaman Liton, over crimes against humanity including the killings of two people during the July 2024 uprising in Rajshahi.
The tribunal also issued arrest warrants against 34 accused and ordered four others to be produced before it.
A three-member bench of International Crimes Tribunal-2, headed by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, passed the orders on Tuesday, following a prosecution petition.
Prosecutor Zahirul Amin represented the state, assisted by prosecutors Faruk Ahmed, Moinul Karim, Marzina Raihan, Shahidul Islam Sardar and Tarek Abdullah.
During the hearing, Prosecutor Zahirul presented details of the allegations and showed three videos to the tribunal. The prosecution claimed the footage showed several accused firing weapons, and identified some of them.
The prosecution then sought to have the charges taken up, along with arrest warrants for the absconding accused and production warrants for those already in custody.
After the hearing, the tribunal issued arrest warrants for 34 accused and ordered four others to be produced before it. The next hearing is scheduled for September 17.
Four ordered to be produced The four accused facing production warrants are former Rajshahi-3 MP Mohammad Asaduzzaman Asad, Dablu Sarker, Zahirul Islam Rubel and Mohaiminul Islam Manik.
34 face arrest warrants
The 34 accused are AHM Khairuzzaman Liton, Biplab Bijoy Talukdar, Humayun Kabir, Rocky Kumar Ghosh, Rashik Dutta, Bappi Chowdhury Rony, Mahidul Islam Mostafa, Khalid Hasan Biplab, Rashedul Karim Rozel, Mehedi Hasan alias Rony, Jedu Sarker alias Jabedur Rahman, Abdul Hamid Sarker alias Tekon, Anwar Hossain alias Anar, Arman Ali, Abdul Momin, Shahadat Hossain Shahu, Touhidul Haque Sumon, Mahtab Hossain Chowdhury, Alauddin alias Alal, Shariful Islam Babu, Mohammad Nabil Hasan, Mahmudul Hasan Rajib, Farhad Hossain Biplab, Taurid Al Masud Rony, Mehedi Hasan Rimel alias Rigen, Ashraful Islam Jafar, Sukanta Kumar Das, Faisal Ahmed Runu, Nur Mohammad Siam, Asadullah-Hil-Galib, Golam Kibria, Alal Parvez Lulu, Moniruzzaman Khan alias Monir and Shafiquzzaman alias Shafiq.
The prosecution filed the formal charges against the 38 accused on July 30. The tribunal took cognizance of the charges on Tuesday.
Allegations

item.title: BIP: Unplanned urbanisation pushes Dhaka near bottom of livability index
item.description:
Dhaka now ranks 171st among 173 cities on the Global Livability Index, planners said Tuesday warning that unplanned urbanisation, environmental degradation and weak governance have pushed the capital to one of the lowest livability levels in the world.
Speaking at a press conference titled "Dhaka City's Livability: Challenges and Roadmap for Planned Solutions," organised by the Bangladesh Institute of Planners (BIP) at its conference hall in Planners Tower, BIP President Muhammad Ariful Islam said transport, air and noise pollution, waterlogging, shrinking green space, public health risks and weak social inclusion are all directly tied to the city's planning failures.
He said Dhaka ranks 18th among the world's most polluted cities.
Of the roughly 56 canals the city once had, only 26 survive in any recognisable form, while 48 areas have been identified as waterlogging-prone due to encroachment on canals and wetlands and poor drainage, he said.
Ariful Islam said unplanned billboards and lighting are damaging the cityscape and road safety, he added, while rising building density and poor waste management are fuelling dengue and chikungunya risks.
Only 7.99 percent of the city's 99.29 square kilometres is green space, he said, far short of what a livable city needs.
On transport, Ariful said Dhaka loses about 50 lakh working hours annually to congestion, at an estimated economic cost of Tk 37,000 crore.
He said around 1,765 tonnes of waste, 27 percent of total generation, goes uncollected daily, worsening waterlogging and mosquito breeding.
BIP General Secretary Mohammad Mosleh Uddin Hasan said Dhaka is heading toward its lowest-ever livability level due to poor implementation of existing plans and institutional weakness.
Planner Adil Muhammad Khan raised concerns over footpath encroachment, illegal businesses, extortion, and political influence in urban management while planner AKM Riaz Uddin noted that despite declining livability, migration to Dhaka continues because other regions lack jobs and services.
Speakers agreed that Dhaka's crisis stems from interlinked failures in environment, land use, transport, health and waste management, calling for long-term, coordinated national planning.

item.title: HSBC launches Export Excellence Awards 2026
item.description:
The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (HSBC) in Bangladesh has officially launched the 10th edition of its flagship 'HSBC Export Excellence Awards 2026' to recognize and honor Bangladeshi exporters for their contributions to the nation’s sustainable economic growth.
The announcement was made during a press conference held at the Pan Pacific Sonargaon Dhaka.
The awards program will recognize high-performing businesses across four distinct categories based on annual export revenue thresholds:
Organized in partnership with the Ministry of Commerce and the British High Commission Dhaka, the awards will utilize Ernst & Young (EY) as an independent technical auditing partner.
Final selections will be evaluated by a joint jury board comprising representatives from HSBC’s senior leadership, the Ministry of Commerce, and the British High Commission.
Candidates will be assessed on financial performance, national economic contribution, operational diversity, corporate governance, regulatory compliance, and sustainable business practices.
Speaking at the launch, Md Mahbub ur Rahman, chief executive officer of HSBC Bangladesh, emphasized that the initiative honors trailblazing enterprises redefining the global footprint of "Made in Bangladesh" through innovation, quality, and long-term sustainability.
Talukdar Noman Anwar, country head of communications at HSBC Bangladesh, detailed the program's guidelines and entry criteria.
The press conference featured a discussion on Bangladesh's evolving export landscape with previous award winners, including Ahsan Khan Chowdhury, chairman & CEO of Pran-RFL Group; Enayetur Rahman, CEO & president of Ulkasemi; and Asif Ashraf, director & CEO of Urmi Group.
The session was also attended by Saiyab Ahmed, deputy director of trade & investment at the British High Commission Dhaka, and Naushad Ekramullah, partner and managing director at EY Bangladesh.
The awards program carries no entry fee or financial purse and is open to all operating enterprises across Bangladesh, regardless of whether they maintain an existing banking relationship with HSBC.
Eligible businesses and third-party nominators can submit entries online through the official portal ( www.business.hsbc.com .bd/EEA2026) until the nomination deadline on September 20, 2026.

item.title: AIUB hosts first-ever ‘QS Bangladesh Forum 2026’
item.description:
The first-ever QS Bangladesh Forum 2026 was held on Monday, August 17, at the Sheraton Dhaka, with the aim of advancing the future of higher education in Bangladesh, strengthening global standards, and enhancing the position of Bangladeshi universities in the international arena.
The forum was hosted by the American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB) and organized by QS (Quacquarelli Symonds), with support from the University Grants Commission of Bangladesh (UGC) and the Association of Private Universities of Bangladesh (APUB).
Themed “Benchmark Bangladesh: Building World-Class Universities Through Global Standards,” the forum brought together key stakeholders from Bangladesh’s higher education sector.
The inaugural session was attended by Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon, MP, as chief guest.
Prof Mamun Ahmed, chairman of the University Grants Commission of Bangladesh, attended as guest of honour.
In his address, the minister highlighted the need to introduce PhD programs at private universities and indicated that initiatives would soon be taken in this regard.
Questioning why private universities should not be permitted to offer PhD programs, he emphasized the importance of creating broader opportunities for advanced research in the private higher education sector.
Referring to the development of private universities in Bangladesh since 1992, he stressed that, by 2026, the country must create greater opportunities for advanced research at private universities.
Highlighting the importance of research, he said that Bangladesh needs cross-border education and stronger research capacity in private universities.
He also noted that the country has no shortage of teachers and researchers, with thousands of researchers contributing to national development through knowledge, expertise, and “Made in Bangladesh” capabilities.
Prof Mamun Ahmed, chairman of UGC, said that Bangladeshi private universities still have significant room for improvement in global university rankings.
He emphasized the need for universities to take a leading role in improving academic quality and making their institutions more attractive to students. Such efforts, he noted, could help attract more international students to Bangladesh for higher education.
QS representatives also addressed the forum, including Ashwin Fernandes, vice president – strategic and international engagement, QS; Jason Newman, chief commercial officer, QS; and Rami Awad, director of regional partnerships, QS.
The welcome address was delivered by Ishtiaque Abedin, founding member of the board of trustees of AIUB and secretary general of APUB.
Md Sabur Khan, president of APUB, also addressed the forum.
The vote of thanks was delivered by Nadia Anwar, founding member and chairperson of the board of trustees, AIUB.
Following the inaugural session, three dedicated sessions were held on QS Rankings Methodology, QS ranking landscape of Bangladesh, and the QS Rankings 2028 Cycle.
The forum also featured two high-level panel discussions involving Vice-Chancellors from leading universities across Bangladesh: “From Campus to Capability: Closing Bangladesh’s Future Skills Gap in the AI Era” and “Accelerating Digital Transformation in Higher Education.”
The panel discussions focused on the future skills required by students in the age of artificial intelligence, aligning education with industry needs, leveraging technology in higher education, and accelerating digital transformation across universities.
The closing session featured a vote of thanks by Carmen Zita Lamagna, former vice chancellor, academic adviser, and member of the board of trustees, AIUB.
The QS Bangladesh Forum 2026 placed particular emphasis on the internationalization of higher education, enhancing the global visibility of research, improving student outcomes and capabilities, and strengthening international partnerships.
With the QS World University Rankings 2028 cycle ahead, discussions also focused on developing a common, practical, and strategic roadmap for universities to prepare for and improve their global competitiveness.

item.title: Jamuna Bank joins BB’s Tk10,000cr agriculture refinance scheme
item.description:
Jamuna Bank PLC has joined Bangladesh Bank’s Tk10,000 crore refinance scheme aimed at boosting agricultural production, strengthening food security and supporting the rural economy.
A participation agreement was signed between Bangladesh Bank and Jamuna Bank PLC on August 16.
Under the three-year revolving refinance scheme, financing will be available for a wide range of agriculture and rural activities, including crop production, fisheries, livestock, agricultural and irrigation machinery, and other income-generating activities.
Eligible farmers and customers will be able to access financing at a maximum simple interest rate of 8% per annum.
The agreement was signed by AKM Saiduzzaman, director, Agricultural Credit Department-2, Bangladesh Bank.
On Jamuna Bank’s behalf, deputy managing director & CRO Md Shahidul Islam and Md Abu Bakkar Siddique, head of agricultural loan, were present at the program.
Md Sakhawat Hossain, joint director-2, and Rafia Sultana, additional director of Bangladesh Bank’s Agricultural Credit Department, were also present at the ceremony.
Through its participation in the scheme, Jamuna Bank aims to expand access to affordable financing for farmers and rural entrepreneurs, helping increase agricultural production, generate employment and contribute to sustainable rural development.

item.title: Hop Lun partners with Brac Healthcare to host employee wellness camp
item.description:
Hop Lun Apparel Limited recently organized a comprehensive ‘Seasonal Disease Prevention and Awareness Session’ at its factory premises in partnership with Brac Healthcare.
The initiative provided workers with free medical check-ups as well as expert guidance on disease prevention, hygiene, and healthy living in order to safeguard their overall health and well-being.
During the session, workers underwent screenings for blood sugar, blood pressure and oxygen saturation levels.
Any individuals diagnosed with adverse health conditions were immediately provided medical treatment by Hop Lun’s in-house medical team.
Additionally, two healthcare professionals from Brac healthcare conducted interactive sessions with the workers, advising workers on preventing common illnesses, knowing when to consult a doctor, and effective ways to maintain overall health at home and in the workplace.
They discussed about how health and work are deeply connected and how personal physical fitness is key to both professional performance and personal life.
Dr Tahmid Hasan Probad, manager, QA and patient experience at Brac Healthcare Ltd, stated: “Through this partnership, we wanted to deliver quality healthcare access for workers and create health awareness among them. We firmly believe that a healthy worker thrives in the workplace with greater ease.”
Gulshan Ara, social initiatives head, Hop Lun Bangladesh, added: “The physical and mental well-being of our workers is one of our top priorities. With this initiative, we aimed to make essential medical support more accessible for our workers and to equip them with the knowledge they need in order to maintain proper health.”
Hop Lun Apparel Limited remains dedicated to prioritizing worker well-being and continuing such health and welfare initiatives across its facilities in the future.

item.title: Bangladesh, IOM launch new initiative to combat cyber-enabled human trafficking
item.description:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM-UN Migration) and the Economic Relations Division (ERD) of Ministry of Finance of Bangladesh have signed a 24-month project to strengthen Bangladesh's efforts to prevent and respond to human trafficking facilitated through digital technologies.
The project, "Countering Cyber-Enabled Human Trafficking Through Technology", funded by the IOM Development Fund, will be implemented by IOM Bangladesh in partnership with the Ministry of Home Affairs. The project aims to support longer-term efforts to prevent cyber-enabled human trafficking in Bangladesh. Its findings and training resources are expected to contribute to future policy and program development and to strengthen existing national and inter-agency efforts to combat trafficking, said a press release on Monday.
Responding to growing concerns over the use of social media, online platforms, job portals and other digital technologies by traffickers to target, recruit, control and exploit people, the project will focus on three key areas including building evidence and knowledge, strengthening law enforcement capacity and improving digital literacy in communities. The agreement was signed by Md Shahriar Kader Siddiky, secretary of ERD, and Dr Laura Tomm Bonde, chief of mission of IOM Bangladesh, in the presence of AKM Sohel, additional secretary and wing chief of UN Wing, ERD, and representatives of relevant government agencies including Ministry of Home Affairs and IOM, according to an ERD press release.
"Technology is transforming the way people communicate, seek employment and connect with opportunities, but it can also be exploited by traffickers," said Dr Laura Tomm Bonde. "This project will help strengthen the evidence, skills and community awareness needed to ensure that technology becomes part of the solution rather than a tool for exploitation," she added.
"The project will contribute to the Government of Bangladesh's efforts to prevent the misuse of technology for human trafficking while promoting technology as a means to counter human trafficking. Its overall outcome is to enable government stakeholders and communities to take informed action to prevent, respond to and mitigate the risks of cyber-enabled human trafficking," Md Shahriar Kader Siddiky emphasized.

item.title: Chamber court upholds bail for ex-chief justice Khairul Haque
item.description:
The Appellate Division’s Chamber Judge Court has upheld the High Court’s bail order for former chief justice A B M Khairul Haque in a case filed under the attempted murder and Explosives Act over violence during the July 2024 mass uprising.
Chamber Judge of the Appellate Division Justice Md Rezaul Haque passed a “no order” on Monday on a state petition seeking a stay on the High Court’s bail order.
Following the order, Khairul Haque’s lawyers said there is no longer any legal impediment to his release from jail.
Senior lawyer Motahar Hossain Saju appeared for Khairul Haque, assisted by lawyers Monayem Nabi Shaheen and others.
Earlier, on August 10, a High Court bench comprising Justice K M Zahid Sarwar and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher granted Khairul Haque bail in the case filed at Banani Police Station over the July uprising.
Khairul Haque was arrested from his Dhanmondi residence on July 24, 2025. He was later shown arrested in a case over the killing of Jubo Dal activist Abdul Qayyum Ahad in Jatrabari during the uprising and subsequently in several other cases.

item.title: 3 sentenced to death for killing AIUB student in Narayanganj
item.description:
A Narayanganj court on Monday sentenced three muggers to death for killing Wazed Alam Shimanto, a student of American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB), in 2024.
Narayanganj District and Sessions’ Judge Abu Shamim Azad pronounced the verdict.
The condemned convicts are Anik, Akash Khan and Chandi Babu.
According to the prosecution, three muggers intercepted Shimanto, a 2nd year student of the AIUB Department of Computer Science, in front of Morgan Girls’ High School at Deubhog of Narayanganj city around 6:00am on December 12, 2024.
At one stage, the hoodlums stabbed Shimanto indiscriminately and left the place after snatching his bag and mobile phone set.
The victim was sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries two days later.
Shimanto’s father Hazi Alam filed a case at Sadar Police Station in this regard.
Police arrested the trio from different parts of the district following the incident. All of them gave confessional statements before the court under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

item.title: PM’s Adviser: 'Mob culture' will not be tolerated
item.description:
The government will not tolerate “mob culture” in the country and will enforce law to prevent such incidents, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Public Administration Affairs Ismail Zabihullah said on Monday.
“Mob culture is undesirable whenever it occurs. We hope there will be no mob culture, and it should never happen,” he said while responding to questions from journalists at an exchange of views at the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon to mark 180 days of the government.
Asked about allegations that mob incidents continued after the ouster of Sheikh Hasina and that law enforcement agencies remained largely inactive in dealing with such incidents, the adviser said he had no clear example of a recent incident of the kind seen during the final period the interim government.
“There is no such mob culture as was seen toward the end of the interim government. However, we can assure you that this kind of mob culture will not be tolerated,” said Zabihullah, also a BNP Standing Committee member.
He stressed that the country would be governed according to law and that the government would enforce it.
Prime Minister’s Political Adviser and another BNP Standing Committee member Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, who joined the discussion, said the extent of mob culture has declined significantly.
He said such a culture emerged partly because of political support and that there had often been an indirect political influence behind such incidents.
“As the rule of law becomes stronger, mob violence will decline,” Rizvi said, adding that the government’s commitment to the rule of law would help create an environment in which such incidents would decrease further.
Prime Minister’s Office spokesperson Mahadi Amin presented statistics on the government’s activities and achievements over the past 180 days.
The event was moderated by Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Saleh Shibli. PM’s Political Adviser Nazrul Islam Khan, Political Adviser Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapan and Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon also spoke at the program.
Ministers and advisers responded to questions from journalists on various issues.
State Minister for Local Government Mir Shahe Alam, State Ministe for Information and Broadcasting Yaser Khan Chowdhury, Foreign Affairs Adviser Humaiun Kobir, Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman, Prime Minister’s Special Assistant on Health SM Ziauddin Haider, Special Assistant on Environment, Forest and Climate Affairs Saimum Parvez and Chief Coordinator at the Prime Minister’s Office Prof SM Abdul Awal, among others, attended the program.

The festival was inaugurated by Imran Haider, High Commissioner of Pakistan to Bangladesh, together with Zain Aziz, trade and investment attaché, and other officials of the Pakistan High Commission.
Representatives from leading media organizations, food bloggers and influencers were also invited to attend the inauguration.

The buffet features favourites from different regions of Pakistan, including Nalli Pulao, Kabuli Pulao, Chicken Sanawari, Mutton Shajahani Handi, Beef Namkeen, Fish Hyderabadi Masala, Chicken Sindhi Biryani, Chicken Lahori Biryani, Chicken Yakhni Pulao and Peshawari Naan, along with many more traditional dishes.
A major attraction is the live cooking station, where famous Pakistani kebabs are freshly prepared and grilled for guests.
Alongside the Pakistani specialties, Summerfields’ continental and international buffet selections will also be available, offering an extensive dining experience for every palate.
The culinary experience has been curated to showcase the iconic flavours of Pakistan, with particular attention to traditional cooking techniques, aromatic spices and authentic regional recipes.
The festival aims not only to offer an exceptional dining experience but also to celebrate the cultural connection between Bangladesh and Pakistan through food and hospitality.

The midfielder, who won the Ballon d'Or in 2024, has struggled with injuries over the past two seasons but shone as Spain won their second World Cup.
Barca's Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong is set to miss several months through injury, encouraging the club to move for Rodri.
The Spain captain was a vital figure for Pep Guardiola at City, leading them to the 2023 Champions League and four Premier League titles among 12 major trophies.

item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon has said the government is constructing modern information complex in every division.
The program will also be expanded at district and upazila level, he said while inaugurating the construction work of the modern Barisal Divisional Information Complex at Ichhakathi in Kashipur of Barisal city on Sunday.
The event was organized by the Department of Mass Communication under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
The information complexes will multifaceted centers for information, knowledge, entertainment and research, he said.
“The complexes will not only be eye-catching buildings; they will serve as hubs of information, knowledge and research. The complexes will primarily function as Digital Information Service Centers, providing a wide range of digital services to the public,” he said.
Swapon said development work under the project is already underway in 26 districts. To popularize the facilities and encourage students to engage in research, promotional leaflets will be distributed to local educational institutions through the ministry, he said.
“The government’s objective is not limited to infrastructure development; rather, it aims to bring the quality of the complexes up to international standard,” he said.
To achieve this, Swapon said, both infrastructure engineering and software engineering are being given separate and equal importance.
Highlighting the technological facilities planned for the complexes, Swapon said they would feature state-of-the-art, technology-enabled cineplexes and electronic screens, with facilities for screening digital movies as well as 3D and 4D films.
Speaking as chair of the event, Secretary of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Mahbuba Farjana said the information complexes would play important role in combating misinformation and disinformation.
Barisal Divisional Commissioner Khalil Ahmed, Barisal City Corporation Administrator Advocate Bilkis Akter Jahan Shirin, spoke among others on the occasion.
In his welcome address, Project Director Moniruzzaman said the seven-storey modern Information Complex in Barisal is being constructed at a cost of Taka 17.63 crore.
Later, Deputy Project Director Rezaur Rabbi Moni presented details of the project through a multimedia presentation.

item.title: Model Ridhika Ridhi’s boyfriend sent to jail in suicide abetment case
item.description:
Model Ridhika Ridhi’s boyfriend, Hasibur Rahman, has been sent to jail in a case filed over her death at her Bashundhara Residential Area home in Dhaka. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mahbub Alam passed the order on Sunday, said Prosecution Department Sub-Inspector Kamal Hossain.
Family members found Ridhi hanging from a ceiling fan in her bedroom on Saturday morning. She was rushed to Kurmitola General Hospital where doctors declared her dead.
Ridhi’s mother Moni Begum filed a case on the same day, accusing Hasibur of abetting her daughter’s suicide.
Hasibur, who had visited Ridhi’s home that day, was arrested from the spot.
On Sunday, Vatara police Sub-Inspector Abdul Wadud, the investigating officer, produced Hasibur before the court and sought his detention in jail.
In the petition, police said preliminary interrogation and investigation had yielded sufficient evidence supporting the allegations against Hasibur. They said he had confessed to the offence and admitted his involvement during questioning.
Police also expressed concern that he might flee if released on bail.
Hasibur’s lawyer, Golam Kibria Choton, sought bail and requested a hearing on Tuesday. The court sent Hasibur to jail and fixed Tuesday for the bail hearing. Police said Ridhi had been on a video call with Hasibur when the incident occurred. Although the death initially appeared to be a suicide, investigators are probing the circumstances to determine the exact cause of death.
Ridhi, who worked as a model, also acted in several dramas, including Ekhane Manush Bikri Hoy, Bahurupi, Double Honeymoon and Sundori.

item.title: Family Card brings relief to some, leaves Korail slum’s poorest behind
item.description:
Ahead of the 13th parliamentary election, the BNP pledged in its election manifesto to introduce the Family Card programme to strengthen the economic security of people, particularly women.
The government launched the pilot programme on March 10 at the T&T playground in Banani, adjacent to Dhaka’s Korail slum. Under the pilot programme, selected women receive Tk 2,500 a month through mobile financial services or bank accounts.
Since then, “Family Card” has become a familiar term among Korail residents. While the programme has brought relief to some families, many of the slum’s poorest residents say they have been left out.
Residents interviewed by Dhaka Tribune alleged that some relatively well-off households received the cards, while families struggling to afford even basic food were denied the benefit.
Rasheda, Morzina among those left out
Rasheda Begum, originally from Rangpur, has lived in Korail for more than a decade. With no homestead in her village, the slum has become her last refuge. She has two children, Tabassum and Zakaria. Tabassum has a disability. Rasheda begs on the streets and in the alleys around Mohakhali to support her children. Her husband left her after their child was born with a disability.
Despite applying for a Family Card, she did not receive one.
A similar story was shared by Morzina Khatun and her son Majnu, both of whom have physical disabilities. They have no homestead in their village and have lived in Korail for around 20 years.
Unable to walk, Morzina begs while sitting on a two-wheeled cart.
Rasheda and Morzina told Dhaka Tribune that officials collected their national ID details and photographs before the pilot programme began, but they received neither cards nor payments.
They alleged that many families with relatively better incomes received cards, while those struggling to afford three meals a day were left out.
“I eat when I can beg. Otherwise, I have to go without food,” Morzina said.
Rasheda said she had contemplated suicide because of poverty but was staying alive for her helpless children. Better-off families among beneficiaries
There is a contrasting picture in Korail, with some residents who appear relatively financially secure also receiving Family Cards.
Nasima Begum is one of them. Her husband, Ashraful, works as a school van driver. Nasima has a two-storey tin-roofed house in the slum with seven rooms, which she rents out for around Tk 5,000 each, earning about Tk 35,000 a month.
“I have received four months’ payments through the Family Card. But I have not received the payments for July and August yet,” she told Dhaka Tribune.
Poorest residents demand inclusion
During a visit to Beltola Adarsh Nagar in Korail on Saturday afternoon, this correspondent found tin-roofed shacks lining narrow lanes. Most homes are so cramped that there is barely enough space to stand inside.
Women in most households work as domestic workers or in garment factories. Many families have several children. In some households, husbands do not support their families, while in others, even the combined income of both spouses is insufficient to make ends meet.
For such families, the Family Card is a much-anticipated source of support.
Under the social safety-net programme, selected families receive cash through mobile financial services. But many households living alongside beneficiaries remain excluded.
Several residents who did not receive cards told Dhaka Tribune that elderly people, widows, persons with disabilities, people suffering from chronic illnesses and families without an earning member should receive priority.
They said only a few such families had received cards, while most remained excluded.
Disabled child, jailed husband leave Sharifa struggling
Sharifa Begum lives in Beltola Adarsh Nagar and works as a domestic helper. Her son Suman has a physical disability. His grandmother looks after him while Sharifa is at work. His father is currently in jail in connection with a case.
“I have done everything short of begging at people’s feet for a Family Card, but no one helped me. My husband is in jail. Even after working in people’s homes, I cannot afford two meals a day. I cannot afford treatment for my disabled child,” Sharifa said, wiping away tears.She appealed to the government for assistance for her son.
Alecha Begum, another extremely poor resident, also did not receive a card. Her husband is ill and unable to work. She earns a living doing domestic work. “I applied for a card but did not get one. Those who are better off got cards, but we did not,” she said.
Another resident, Jharna, said, “My husband’s income is not enough to run the family. I am struggling with two children. We desperately need a card.”
Four months’ payments received, July-August dues remain
Some beneficiaries received Tk 2,500 a month from March through June under the pilot programme, but several said they have yet to receive payments for July and August.
Marium Begum told Dhaka Tribune that she had received four months’ payments through mobile banking but had not received the payments for July and August.
Sharmin Begum said, “I have not received the money for two months, July and August. I went to the office to find out what happened, but they could not give me any information.”
PM to formally launch programme in Kishoreganj
Following the pilot phase, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is scheduled to formally launch the Family Card programme in Kishoreganj on August 16. The launch is scheduled to take place at Ward 8 of Latifabad Union in Kishoreganj Sadar upazila.
Mohammad Rezaur Rahman, deputy director of the Department of Social Services, told Dhaka Tribune that the prime minister would formally launch the programme in Kishoreganj on August 16.
The programme will then be rolled out gradually across all upazilas and unions by the end of October.
Who will receive Family Cards?
Women from extremely poor, poor and low-income households will primarily be eligible for the cards, with extremely poor and poor families receiving priority during the initial phase.
Under the government guidelines, landless and homeless families, households with persons with disabilities, hijra and Bede communities, ethnic minority families and households owning up to 0.5 acres of land will receive priority.
A maximum of five members of each family will be considered for eligibility. In joint families, a separate card will be issued for every five members.

item.title: Building stronger institutions: Shafiqul Alam's role in Bangladesh's governance journey
item.description:
Corporate governance has become one of the defining themes of Bangladesh's corporate sector over the past three decades.
Regulatory reforms, expanding capital markets and growing investors’ expectations have steadily reshaped how companies are expected to operate.
Alongside these changes, a number of professionals have helped translate governance principles into practice.
Md Shafiqul Alam FCA, FCMA, FCS is one of them.
Over the past two decades, his work has spanned audit, financial reporting, governance advisory and professional education, bringing him into close engagement with the boards of directors of public and private companies, regulators and corporate leaders.
Currently serving as managing partner and CEO of Shafiqul Alam & Co., Chartered Accountants, and as council member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Bangladesh (ICAB) for the 2025–2028 term, Alam has been part of the broader conversation on governance standards in Bangladesh.
The introduction of the Corporate Governance Guidelines in 2006 was one of the earliest attempts to establish structured governance expectations for listed companies.
More than a decade later, the Corporate Governance Code introduced in 2018 expanded those expectations and strengthened board oversight, with greater emphasis on independent directors, audit committees, risk management and disclosure standards.
More recently, the Financial Reporting Council's (FRC) initiative to develop a dedicated governance code for non-listed Public Interest Entities (PIEs) has drawn attention to governance practices beyond the listed sector–an area that has remained relatively less regulated despite its significant economic footprint.
These changes have also reshaped the role of directors, senior executives, finance professionals and auditors.
Issues that rarely appeared on boardroom agendas two decades ago, such as cybersecurity, ESG reporting, enterprise risk management, succession planning and board effectiveness, are now regular subjects of discussion.
As governance expectations have evolved, so too has the role of governance professionals.
Alam views corporate governance as more than regulatory compliance.
His professional work reflects the view that governance is about building institutions that are transparent, accountable and capable of sustaining long-term growth.
Good governance, he believes, should become part of an organization's culture rather than a checklist prepared for regulators.
Organizations create lasting value when transparency, ethical leadership, sound risk management and board accountability are embedded in everyday decision-making.
Alongside his professional practice, Alam has remained actively engaged in governance education and capacity building.
Those engagements have included training programs with the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC), Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), Bangladesh Institute of Capital Market (BICM) and the Bangladesh Academy for Securities Markets (BASM).
The programs have brought together directors, senior executives, company secretaries, finance professionals, auditors and market participants to examine the practical application of governance principles and evolving regulatory requirements.
The discussions focused on helping participants understand how governance principles can be applied in day-to-day business decisions rather than treated solely as compliance requirements.
Alam has also been involved in professional discussions on strengthening governance standards for non-listed public interest entities.
While listed companies are already subject to comprehensive governance requirements under the BSEC Corporate Governance Code, many non-listed public interest entities–including large financial institutions, insurers, state-owned enterprises and other significant players–manage substantial public resources without being covered by a dedicated governance framework.
Strengthening governance within these entities, he argues, can improve accountability, enhance financial reporting quality, protect lenders and other stakeholders, and reinforce confidence across the broader financial system.
For Alam, strengthening governance in these entities is ultimately about strengthening the institutions that underpin Bangladesh's economy.
As businesses become larger, more technology-driven and increasingly connected to international markets, governance frameworks must adapt to address emerging issues such as enterprise risk management, cybersecurity, ESG reporting, succession planning and board effectiveness.
Sustainable governance depends not only on well-designed regulations but also on competent professionals capable of implementing those regulations effectively.
Over the years, Alam's work with chartered accountants, company secretaries, finance executives, internal auditors and board members has focused on promoting higher professional standards and encouraging continuous learning.
His work across audit, assurance, financial reporting and board advisory has given him practical exposure to governance practices across a wide range of companies.
This experience has reinforced his view that governance cannot be reduced to documentation alone–effective governance ultimately depends on leadership, ethical decision-making and institutional culture.
Rather than viewing governance as an obstacle to entrepreneurship, he presents it as a framework that enables businesses to grow sustainably while protecting the interests of investors, lenders, employees and society.
Bangladesh's governance journey remains a work in progress. As regulatory expectations continue to evolve and businesses face increasingly complex risks, governance is likely to remain central to corporate decision-making.
Professionals involved in policy, education and advisory services will continue to shape that transition.
Md Shafiqul Alam's career reflects one part of that broader institutional story.

item.title: Tk 1.21C robbery from PM’s cousin’s petrol pump: Five arrested
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch (DB) has arrested five people over the robbery of Tk 1.21 crore from a petrol pump in Uttara, allegedly linked to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s maternal cousin Tasin Akhtar Haque.
Police also recovered RAB-marked vests, fake identity cards, firearms and other equipment allegedly used in the robbery. The suspected mastermind remains at large.
The arrestees are: Md Ilias Shikdar, 36, Jafar, 36, Md Rabiul Islam alias Rubel, 34, Mintu Rari, 23, and Sagar Baroi, 40.
Additional Police Commissioner (DB) Md Shafiqul Islam disclosed the information at a press briefing at the DMP Media Centre on Saturday.
He said four employees of DL Filling Station were carrying Tk 1.21 crore to a bank around 10:30am on August 9 when a group of motorcycle-borne robbers intercepted them near Crown Plaza on the Dhaka-Mymensingh Road.
The robbers allegedly threatened and assaulted them with firearms and machetes before fleeing with the money.
Following the incident, the DB and Uttara Crime Division launched a joint investigation. Acting on intelligence, police arrested Ilias Shikdar and Jafar in Siddhirganj, Narayanganj.
Police later recovered three RAB-marked vests, two caps, fake RAB identity cards, number plates, walkie-talkies, handcuffs, two 7.65mm pistols, three magazines and six rounds of ammunition from Ilias’s rented home in Bandar.
Rubel and Mintu were subsequently arrested in Matuail and Kazlarpar, respectively. Police recovered Tk 3 lakh in stolen cash from Rubel’s residence, while a raid on Mintu’s home yielded four RAB-marked vests, fake RAB IDs, number plates, walkie-talkies, handcuffs, two pistols, three magazines and 15 rounds of ammunition.
Based on information provided by Rubel and Mintu, police arrested Sagar from his rented home in Postogola and recovered Tk 9 lakh in stolen cash. Shafiqul Islam said the stolen money was divided among the gang, with the masterminds taking larger shares and others receiving portions for providing logistical support. Sagar received Tk 9 lakh but had not spent it, he added.
The DB chief said ballistic checks showed that the recovered firearms were not weapons looted from police but had been illegally acquired.
He said the mastermind remains at large and that investigators had found no prior personal connection between the suspect and the victim.
According to police, the gang targeted the petrol pump after learning that several days’ cash had accumulated because banks were closed during the holidays. The group allegedly planned the robbery knowing the money would be deposited once the banks reopened.
Police said efforts are underway to arrest the remaining suspects and recover the rest of the stolen money.

item.title: Bangladesh, Kosovo reaffirm strong opposition to all forms of transnational crimes
item.description:
Recognizing their common commitment to peace, stability, and international security, Bangladesh and Kosovo have reaffirmed their strong opposition to terrorism, violent extremism, and all forms of transnational crime.
They reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the friendly relations between the two countries on the basis of mutual respect, shared values, common interests, and the principles of international law.
The issues of mutual interest were discussed at the second Foreign Office Consultations between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Diaspora of the Republic of Kosovo held in Prishtina recently.
The Bangladeshi delegation was led by Dr M Nazrul Islam, secretary (Bilateral – East & West) of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while the Kosovar delegation was led by Ilir Muçaj, secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Diaspora.
The two sides acknowledged the significant untapped potential for expanding bilateral cooperation in the fields of trade, investment, education, agriculture, information and communication technology, tourism, labour mobility, and people-to-people exchanges.
They agreed to continue working closely to fully utilise the complementarities of their respective economies for mutual benefit.
The two sides reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and expressed satisfaction with the steady progress achieved since the establishment of diplomatic relations, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Both sides welcomed the bilateral instruments concluded thus far and emphasized their importance in strengthening institutional cooperation.
They agreed that bilateral relations would be further enhanced through the early conclusion of the agreements currently under negotiation, particularly those related to economic cooperation, the avoidance of double taxation, and other mutually beneficial areas.
The two sides reaffirmed their commitment to enhancing cooperation at both the bilateral and multilateral levels and agreed to continue close coordination and consultation in regional and international organizations on issues of mutual interest.
The Kosovo side highly appreciated Bangladesh's longstanding contribution to United Nations peacekeeping operations and expressed its sincere gratitude to the members of the Bangladesh to the UN Peace-Keeping Forces who served in Kosovo.
The Bangladeshi side welcomed Kosovo's growing participation in international and regional organizations and initiatives and expressed its support for Kosovo's continued integration into international organizations, conventions, and multilateral mechanisms as an equal participant.
The Kosovo side commended Bangladesh for its humanitarian response to the Rohingya refugee crisis and expressed its support for Bangladesh's efforts aimed at ensuring the safe, voluntary, dignified, and sustainable repatriation of the displaced Rohingya population to Rakhine State in Myanmar.
The Kosovo side also underlined the importance of sustained engagement by the international community to facilitate a durable solution to the crisis.
The two sides recognized the growing demand for labour mobility and underlined the importance of establishing a structured framework for the recruitment and employment of Bangladeshi workers in Kosovo.
They agreed to explore the possibility of developing government-to-government (G2G) cooperation mechanisms that would ensure transparent, orderly, and mutually beneficial labour migration.
The two sides emphasized the importance of maintaining regular Foreign Office Consultations as an effective mechanism for strengthening bilateral cooperation, reviewing progress, and identifying new areas of collaboration.
They agreed to hold the third Foreign Office Consultations in Dhaka during 2027 at a mutually convenient date.
The consultations were held in a constructive atmosphere, reflecting the excellent relations between the Republic of Kosovo and the People's Republic of Bangladesh and their shared commitment to further deepening bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Muddy road causes suffering for Madhupur people
item.description:
A three-kilometre muddy road in Madhupur upazila of Tangail is causing immense suffering for local residents, particularly during the monsoon.
The road, stretching from Pichila Ghona to Momin Ara along the border areas of Ausnara and Mahishmara unions, is yet to be paved or widened despite its importance to the local community.
During the rainy season, several sections of the road become waterlogged and muddy, making it difficult for vehicles and pedestrians to move. The poor condition also severely disrupts the transportation of agricultural produce to markets, leaving farmers to suffer.
Locals said agricultural land and various establishments have developed on both sides of the road. Madhupur’s famous pineapples and other agricultural products are transported to markets using this route. But even a light shower leaves parts of the road submerged and covered in mud, making travel extremely difficult.
Students, patients, traders and pedestrians are among those who face difficulties due to the road’s dilapidated condition. Farmers are particularly affected as they struggle to take their produce to market in time and at reasonable transportation costs.
Abu Hanif, a resident of Haldia village, said the road is extremely important for people in the area. “During the rainy season, the road becomes so bad that even walking becomes difficult. It should be paved without further delay,” he said.
Another resident, Ainal Haque, said a large number of people use the road every day. Farmers, in particular, face serious problems while transporting pineapples and other crops to markets. “If the road is improved, transportation of agricultural products will become easier, and farmers will have a better chance of getting fair prices,” he said.
A resident, Chan Mia, said locals have been demanding repairs for years. “The suffering increases several times once the rainy season begins. If the road is permanently paved, the long-standing problems of the people will be greatly reduced,” he said.
Madhupur Upazila Engineer Rafiqul Islam Bhuiyan said the road from Pichila Ghona to Momin Ara has been sent for inclusion in the government gazette. “Once the road is assigned an ID number and funds are allocated, work will begin,” he said.

All filling stations shut down in Brahmanbaria amid gas crisis
item.description:
All CNG filling stations in Brahmanbaria have been shut down due to a severe gas shortage, causing widespread suffering for passengers and transport workers. Gas supply to the stations was completely suspended from Thursday night, with no clear indication of when services will resume.
According to sources, Bakhrabad Gas Distribution Company Limited had been supplying gas to five filling stations in the district at a reduced rate since Wednesday. Before the crisis, the stations received around 50,000 cubic metres of gas daily, although demand was nearly double that amount.
For more than two weeks, gas pressure at the stations had remained unusually low. Against the normal pressure of 15 PSI, the stations were receiving only 2-3 PSI. Supply was reduced further on Wednesday before being completely suspended on Thursday night.
The shutdown has severely affected CNG-powered vehicles. Many CNG auto-rickshaw drivers have switched to LPG cylinders, resulting in higher fares. Passenger numbers have also fallen as fewer vehicles are operating on roads and highways.
Farid Mia, a passenger, said he waited for an hour at Kumarshil intersection for a CNG auto-rickshaw to travel to Bishwa Road. The driver initially demanded Tk 80, although the regular fare is Tk 40. After bargaining, they agreed on Tk 70.
Rafik Mia, a driver, said the regular fare from Kumarshil intersection to Sarail-Bishwa Road is Tk 50. He had been charging Tk 70 amid the gas shortage and now charges Tk 90 after switching to LPG.
Md Monayem Mia, manager of Khwaja Garib-e-Nawaz Filling Station in Sarail, said the station was forced to close due to the lack of gas. He said Bakhrabad Gas Distribution officials indicated that supply might resume on Sunday or Monday.
Md Shafiqul Haque, deputy general manager of Bakhrabad Gas Distribution's Brahmanbaria office, attributed the crisis to an LNG shortage. He said authorities could not confirm when the situation would improve, though they hoped the crisis would end soon.

item.title: Load shedding halves production at Gopalganj BSCIC Industrial Estate
item.description:
Frequent load shedding has cut industrial production by nearly half at Gopalganj BSCIC Industrial Estate, where factories are experiencing around five hours of power outages during the 11-hour working period each day.
Production at the estate normally runs from 9:00 am to 8:00 pm. As most factories depend heavily on electricity, frequent outages are disrupting production, while owners still have to pay workers their full wages. As a result, industrial units are incurring significant losses, with plastic factories reportedly bearing the brunt.
According to the Executive Engineer’s Office of West Zone Power Distribution Company (WZPDCL) in Gopalganj, the BSCIC feeder has a daily demand of around 2 megawatts, while only 1-1.25 megawatts is being supplied.
Sujan Das, industrial estate officer of Gopalganj BSCIC, said the estate has 74 industrial plots, of which 61 currently have operational units. These include wooden and steel furniture factories, pulse mills, automobile and engineering workshops, polymer industries, oil mills, puffed-rice and sanitary-product manufacturing units.
He said frequent load shedding had reduced production across the estate, while voltage fluctuations were damaging machinery. Factory owners were also paying workers despite production remaining suspended. “We have started working with the relevant authorities to ensure uninterrupted power supply to the BSCIC industrial estate,” he added.
Kazi Hasan, director of Khan Industries, which operates three plastic-related units, said its machines require about two hours to heat up before production can begin. However, electricity often goes off and returns every hour.
“When the power goes out, the machine temperature drops to zero. Raw materials are damaged inside the machines, workers remain idle and production stops. This causes losses on three fronts,” he said.
Hasan said the company’s polymer units had suffered the most. A machine screw worth around Tk 250,000 was damaged and will have to be imported from China, taking about 15 days.
Imam Hasan, director of Sharif Furniture, said voltage fluctuations had caused losses of around Tk 300,000. He said five to six hours of load shedding during the factory’s 11-hour working period had reduced production to about 45%.
“Workers sit idle during outages, but we still have to pay them. Furniture supplies to showrooms have also declined alarmingly,” he said, demanding uninterrupted daytime power.
Bidhan Biswas, proprietor of Moni Engineering Workshop, said hourly outages had severely disrupted production of rice-husking machines and agricultural equipment. Production during the first 12 days of this month had fallen by half.
Lutfar Rahman Luthu, proprietor of Lutfar Rahman Pulses Mill, said power shortages had reduced production and prevented the mill from meeting market demand.
Mohammad Iqbal Hossain, owner of Gopalganj Motors, said electricity was essential for automobile servicing. “Without electricity, almost everything at the BSCIC estate comes to a standstill,” he said.
Mohammad Moin Uddin, executive engineer of WZPDCL’s Gopalganj town electricity supply office, said the town’s nine feeders have a combined demand of 18 megawatts, while only 8 to 9 megawatts are supplied from the national grid.
He said the power situation had started improving on Thursday and assured that special attention would be given to the BSCIC feeder.
