item.title: DMP takes zero-tolerance stance on drugs, snatching
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed has directed police to adopt a zero-tolerance approach to drug-related crimes, take effective measures to prevent illegal activities at hotels and spa centres, and maintain round-the-clock surveillance in snatching-prone areas.
He gave the directives at the monthly crime review meeting for July 2026, held at the Bangladesh Police Auditorium in Rajarbagh in the capital on Thursday. The DMP commissioner instructed police to strengthen intelligence activities alongside regular drives against drug dealers and others involved in drug-related crimes.
He also directed officials concerned to take necessary measures to prevent illegal activities at hotels and spa centres within their respective police station areas. “If information about such activities is received, immediate legal action should be taken while maintaining regular surveillance,” he said.
To prevent snatching, Mosleh Uddin instructed the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit and Detective Branch (DB) to maintain round-the-clock field presence in coordination with the Crime Division after identifying snatching-prone areas.
He also ordered stronger intelligence surveillance, patrols and operations in those areas and directed the units concerned to work in coordination to bring the criminals to justice.
The DMP chief further asked the officers-in-charge of the relevant police stations and senior officials of the Crime Division to visit the scene of every crime. He stressed the importance of visiting crime scenes in person, collecting necessary evidence and properly examining the circumstances surrounding incidents to establish the facts and make investigations more effective.
Mosleh Uddin also directed field-level police officials to discharge their duties with the highest professionalism, responsibility and dedication to control crime and ensure the safety of city residents.

item.title: JMB member arrested in Savar sent to court
item.description:
Police sent an alleged member of banned militant outfit JMB to court on Thursday, seeking a 10-day remand in a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act.
The accused, identified as Mohammad Arif, 26, was arrested by members of the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit from Hemayetpur in Savar on Tuesday. He was produced before the court from Savar Model Police Station around noon on Thursday.
According to police, several bombs were recovered from a bag in Arif’s possession at the time of his arrest. Later, based on information provided by him, police raided his rented residence in South Shyampur, Hemayetpur.
During the raid, police recovered several powerful bombs, cocktails and a large quantity of materials allegedly used to make explosives.
Police subsequently filed a case at Savar Model Police Station under the Anti-Terrorism Act, naming six people, including Arif, and several unidentified others as accused.
According to the case statement, the accused are members of the banned New JMB and had gathered in the Savar area with explosives to carry out acts of sabotage.
The statement also alleged that they supported the ideology of the banned organisation and were involved in activities aimed at creating public panic, threatening public safety and national sovereignty, and attempting to attack law enforcement personnel.
The other named accused are currently absconding, police said.
Savar Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Saiful Alam said Arif was sent to court with a 10-day remand plea.

item.title: Fakhrul’s presidential nomination sparks celebrations in Thakurgaon
item.description:
Thakurgaon, the birthplace of BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, erupted in celebration after reports that he had been finalized as the party’s candidate for Bangladesh’s 23rd presidential election.
Following a high-level BNP meeting on Thursday, news of Fakhrul’s nomination quickly spread across the district. Party activists and local residents gathered at the BNP office and his ancestral home in Kalibari. Supporters organized celebratory processions, distributed sweets and exchanged greetings, turning parts of the town into a festive scene.
Fakhrul became involved in politics as a student at Dhaka University. He later worked as a college teacher before entering local politics and being elected chairman of Thakurgaon Municipality. He subsequently served as a member of parliament, state minister and full minister.
Over more than a decade of political turbulence, Fakhrul played a significant role in keeping the BNP organized and united. His political career also included periods of imprisonment amid the party’s prolonged political struggles.
Residents described his nomination as a major achievement not only for Thakurgaon but also for the wider northern region.
Prof Abu Bakar Siddique, former principal of Thakurgaon Government Women’s College, described Fakhrul as one of the region’s most distinguished figures. He expressed hope that development initiatives for Thakurgaon would receive greater momentum if Fakhrul assumes the presidency.
Dr ABM Khairul Kabir, president of the Thakurgaon chapter of the Bangladesh Medical Association and a former director of Dinajpur Medical College Hospital, said Fakhrul’s achievement was a source of pride for the entire northern region.
District BNP President Mirza Faisal Amin said the family was deeply moved, calling the nomination recognition of Fakhrul’s lifelong sacrifice, dedication and integrity.
Residents expressed hope that, if elected president, Fakhrul would strengthen democratic institutions and help reflect the hopes and aspirations of ordinary citizens.

item.title: CUET declares campus ponds, ditches hazardous after 3 student drownings
item.description:
Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) has declared all campus ponds and ditches hazardous and banned students from bathing or swimming in them following the drowning of three students.
The directive was issued in a notice signed by Professor Saiful Islam, director of the Directorate of Students’ Welfare, on Thursday.
The notice said all campus ponds had been declared hazardous in the interest of students’ safety. Until further notice, entering, swimming or otherwise going into any campus pond is strictly prohibited.
Violators will be considered to have breached university discipline and face disciplinary action under the university’s rules, the notice said.
CUET currently has two ponds and several ditches on its campus. The decision came after three students drowned in one of the ponds in recent weeks.
On Wednesday, second-year students Chomok Dutta of the Computer Science and Engineering Department and Shanto Deb of the Electrical and Electronic Engineering Department drowned while bathing in the pond.
Earlier, on July 28, fourth-year Mechanical Engineering student Arnab Saha drowned in the same pond.
According to CUET sources, Shanto and Arnab had entered the pond beside Kazi Nazrul Islam Hall to bathe with friends. They were submerged at one point and later rescued and taken to hospital, where doctors declared them dead.
The latest deaths occurred just two weeks after Arnab’s drowning, leaving the university community in mourning once again.

item.title: Fertilizer sales irregularities grip Rajshahi, farmers protest
item.description:
Farmers across the Rajshahi region are struggling to buy subsidised fertiliser at government-fixed prices, amid allegations of hoarding, diversion and an organised syndicate involving dealers and unauthorised retailers.
The crisis comes as Aman planting is underway, raising concerns among farmers that delays in getting fertiliser could affect crop yields.
Farmers allege that some dealers sell fertiliser allocation orders to black-market traders even before receiving supplies. Others reportedly sell fertiliser directly to retailers from warehouses instead of distributing it through designated outlets. There are also allegations that fertiliser allocated to one district or upazila is being diverted to another.
During visits to several rural areas of Rajshahi, most authorised dealers were found without subsidised fertiliser, while nearby retail shops were selling the same products at significantly higher prices.
Under government-fixed rates, a 50kg bag of triple super phosphate (TSP) costs Tk1,350 and a bag of diammonium phosphate (DAP) Tk1,050. Farmers, however, said they were paying Tk1,700–1,800 for TSP and around Tk1,600 for DAP because of shortages at authorised outlets.
“I have a farmer’s card. I went to authorised dealers several times but could not buy fertiliser,” said Russel Hossain, a farmer from Baraikuri village in Paba upazila.
“Fertiliser is not available at the government-fixed price. But if you are willing to pay more, there is no shortage.”
At M/s Haque & Sons Enterprise, an authorised Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) dealer at Nowhata Bazar in Paba, no subsidised fertiliser was available during the visit.
Dealer Abdul Haque said he supplies fertiliser to several thousand farmers across 42 mouzas.
“In July, I received only 22 bags of TSP, 70 bags of MOP and 110 bags of DAP. The supplies were exhausted within two or three days,” he said.
An employee of Tasnim Enterprise, another authorised dealer, also said the shop’s fertiliser stock had run out. However, shop owner Fazlur Rahman later said fertiliser was available and claimed the employee had provided incorrect information.
At a nearby retail shop, an employee offered to sell a 50kg bag of DAP for Tk1,600, Tk550 above the government-fixed price. He said the shop collected fertiliser from various sources and claimed subsidised fertiliser passed through three or four middlemen before reaching retailers.
Farmers have long alleged that a syndicate involving dishonest dealers, unauthorised retailers and officials responsible for monitoring fertiliser distribution is controlling the market.
Several farmers, speaking on condition of anonymity, alleged that field-level agricultural officials were involved in the network. They also claimed that hundreds of unauthorised fertiliser retailers were operating as part of the system.
Sajedur Rahman, a farmer from Chhoto Palashi village in Rishikul Union of Tanore, said farmers could not find fertiliser at government-fixed prices.
“When we go to the dealers, they say there is no fertiliser. We are forced to buy from high-priced retail shops,” he said.
Farmers in Palashi said TSP was selling for Tk1,700–1,800 per bag, while DAP was available for around Tk1,600. MOP, officially priced at Tk1,050, was reportedly being sold for about Tk500 more.
Despite the allegations, officials said they had not received complaints about a fertiliser shortage.
Azizur Rahman, deputy director of the Department of Agricultural Extension in Rajshahi division, said, “We have not received any complaints from farmers about a fertiliser shortage. Aman planting is underway everywhere, and agricultural officials are advising farmers.”
Kazi Shahidul Islam, Rajshahi district administrator and chairman of the district fertiliser distribution committee, said he had not received complaints about higher prices but promised to investigate.
According to Agriculture Ministry data, Rajshahi received higher allocations of TSP, DAP and MOP in July and August this year than during the same period in 2025.
The combined allocation rose from 5,876 tonnes in July 2025 to 7,033 tonnes in July 2026. August allocations also increased, with TSP rising from 1,430 tonnes to 1,511 tonnes, DAP from 2,404 tonnes to 2,647 tonnes and MOP from 1,709 tonnes to 1,760 tonnes.
Nasir Uddin, assistant director (fertiliser) at the BADC Rajshahi office, said the agency was distributing fertiliser according to the quantities approved by the Agriculture Ministry. He added that seasonal demand had increased because some farmers were applying fertiliser beyond recommended doses.
The Rajshahi agricultural region, comprising Rajshahi, Natore, Naogaon and Chapainawabganj, has set a target of cultivating Aman rice on 410,000 hectares. About 40% of the targeted area had been planted as of Wednesday.
Meanwhile, farmers in Chapainawabganj’s Gomastapur upazila staged a protest on Wednesday after failing to obtain adequate fertiliser from dealers.
Farmers from Rahonpur Union gathered at the upazila parishad premises and later met Upazila Nirbahi Officer Zillur Rahman.
They said fertiliser was unavailable during a critical stage of Aman cultivation and warned that delays could reduce crop yields.
Gomastapur Upazila Agriculture Officer Saklain Hossain said officials were monitoring the supply situation and would take action if problems were found.
UNO Zillur Rahman said necessary measures were being taken to ensure farmers received fertiliser at government-fixed prices. He warned that legal action would be taken against anyone found selling fertiliser above the fixed price, hoarding supplies to create an artificial shortage, or harassing farmers.

Strong assurances received on renewal of Ganges Water Sharing Treaty
item.description:
The Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Water Resources was informed on Thursday that strong assurances have been received regarding the renewal of the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty between Bangladesh and India, commonly known as the Farakka Treaty.
The committee was also informed that the main implementation work of the Teesta Master Plan is expected to begin next year.
The first meeting of the committee on the Ministry was held at the National Parliament with committee chairman Mohammad Shofiqul Haque Milon MP presiding.
The committee discussed various initiatives including advance preparaFtions to prevent river erosion and tree plantation programs.
The meeting was informed that the Padma Barrage Project has already been approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC).
A presentation was made before the committee on the overall activities of the Ministry of Water Resources including ongoing development programs, project progress, implementation periods and allocations.
According to the presentation, 93 development projects are currently being implemented under the ministry. A total of Tk 7,832.80 crore has been allocated for these projects in the 2026-27 fiscal year.
The committee called for completing the development projects within their stipulated timelines, ensuring proper and efficient use of allocated funds and taking more effective measures to improve public services.
The Ganges Water Sharing Treaty was signed by Bangladesh and India on Dec 12, 1996 for 30 years and is due to expire in December 2026.
The treaty provides for sharing Ganges water at India’s Farakka Barrage during the dry season from Jan 1 to May 31 each year on the basis of a 10-day schedule.
Under the agreement, when the flow is 70,000 cusecs or less, Bangladesh and India receive 50 percent each. If the flow is between 70,000 and 75,000 cusecs, Bangladesh receives 35,000 cusecs and India gets the remainder. When the flow is 75,000 cusecs or more, India receives 40,000 cusecs and Bangladesh gets the remainder.
With the treaty approaching expiry, its renewal has emerged as a key water-sharing issue between the two countries amid concerns over declining dry-season flows, climate change, rising water demand and downstream ecological impacts.

item.description:
Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) on Thursday submitted the nomination paper on behalf of its Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir for the presidential election.
A BNP delegation led by its Standing Committee Member Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan submitted the nomination paper to Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) A M M Nasir Uddin, the Chief Election Officer for the presidential election, at the Election Building in the city's Agargaon.
BNP Standing Committee Member and Narsingdi-2 constituency lawmaker Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan proposed Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as a presidential candidate in the nomination paper, while BNP Standing Committee Member and Dhaka-3 constituency lawmaker Gayeshwar Chandra Roy supported it.
Earlier on Thursday, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman formally announced Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as the BNP candidate for the presidency at a meeting of the party's Standing Committee.
The prime minister proposed Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir's name for the presidential nomination, and the Standing Committee members unanimously approved the proposal.
The meeting was held today at the meeting room of the Cabinet Division at the Prime Minister's Office in Bangladesh Secretariat.
On August 9, Chief Whip of the Parliament Nurul Islam Moni and BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi collected the nomination paper from the office of the Chief Election Officer.
Earlier, the Election Commission (EC) announced the schedule for the presidential election on August 6. According to the schedule, August 13 was set as the date for submission of nomination papers, while voting will be held on August 20.
Senior Secretary of the EC Secretariat Akhtar Ahmed said the Chief Election Commissioner finalized the schedule in consultation with the Acting Speaker in accordance with Section 5(3) of the Presidential Election Act, 1991.
He said nomination papers could be submitted from 10 am to 4 pm on August 13. The nomination papers will be scrutinized on August 16. The last date for withdrawal of candidacy is August 18 until 4pm. Voting will be held on August 20 from 2pm to 5pm at the session room of Jatiya Sangsad.
Akhtar Ahmed said the voter list for the presidential election has already been prepared.

item.title: PM to attend ‘Rhidoye Dhaka 416’ event at Lalbagh Aug 29
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will attend “Rhidoye Dhaka 416,” the final event marking 416 years of historic Dhaka, at Lalbagh Fort in the capital on August 29.
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator Abdus Salam announced the details at a press conference at Nagar Bhaban on Thursday.
He said the 416th anniversary of historic Dhaka will be celebrated through a range of colorful programs highlighting the city’s rich history and culture.
The special celebration has been organized under the theme “Festival, Pride and Responsibility.”
“The event is being organized with the expectation of reviving Dhaka’s heritage. When people live with Dhaka in their hearts, they will also develop a sense of responsibility to keep the city clean,” Salam said.
He said various programs will be held at different locations across the capital until September 5 as part of the celebrations.
Final event at Lalbagh Fort
The final event will begin at 4pm on August 29 at Lalbagh Fort, the DSCC administrator said.
“Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has kindly agreed to attend the event. The LGRD state minister and the administrator of Dhaka North City Corporation will also be present,” he said.
The event will feature dance performances by children, an exhibition of inventions by young scientists and an exhibition of books written about Dhaka.
There will also be stalls showcasing famous foods from Old Dhaka.
The prime minister will plant a tree and visit Lalbagh Fort during the event. He will inaugurate the program through the release of festoons and balloons, followed by the release of pigeons.
A traditional kite festival celebrating the heritage of Old Dhaka will also be inaugurated at the venue.
The special “Clean Dhaka, Green Dhaka” and mosquito-control campaigns will also be launched on the occasion and subsequently carried out in every ward, Salam said.
A documentary titled “Rhidoye Dhaka” will be screened at the event, while a commemorative book on Dhaka will also be unveiled.
The organizers also hope to unveil a commemorative postage stamp marking Dhaka Day, subject to approval from the relevant ministry.
The celebrations will conclude with a light-and-sound show and a cultural program after a short break, Salam said.

item.title: Four killed as bus collides with leguna in Cox’s Bazar
item.description:
Four people were killed and five others injured after a bus collided head-on with a leguna (Mahindra) in Chakaria upazila of Cox’s Bazar on Thursday morning.
The accident occurred around 6:30am near the Baitul Mamur Jame Mosque area in Nayapara of Khutakhali Union on the Chittagong-Cox’s Bazar Highway, said SI Mohammad Shamsuzzaman of Malumghat Highway Police Station.
The deceased were identified as Mohammad Jasim Uddin, of Segunbagicha village in Khutakhali; Mohammad Shahed, of Fulchhari Shiapara; Mohammad Rafique, of West Gajalia village in Eidgaon; and Mohammad Ziaul Haque, of Notun Office area in the same upazila.
Shahed, Rafique and Ziaul died while undergoing treatment at Cox’s Bazar District Sadar Hospital, while Jasim died at Malumghat Christian Memorial Hospital in the afternoon.
The injured are Syed Alam, his son Mohammad Sarwar, Ziaul Haque, Mohammad Delwar Hossain, and Syed Karim. They were taken to the two hospitals for treatment. Three of the injured were reported to be in critical condition.
According to police and local residents, a Lal Shobuj Paribahan bus was travelling to Cox’s Bazar from Noakhali Sadar, while the leguna was carrying passengers from Eidgaon to Chakaria. The vehicles collided head-on after reaching Nayapara in Khutakhali.
The impact left the leguna badly mangled. Locals rescued the injured and took them to nearby hospitals.
SI Shamsuzzaman said the accident occurred amid heavy rain early in the morning. Police later used a crane to remove the damaged vehicles from the highway, and traffic returned to normal about an hour later.
Police said legal procedures would be completed before the bodies are handed over to the victims’ families.

item.title: Govt moves to formulate policy on battery-run rickshaws
item.description:
The government has taken an initiative to formulate a policy for managing battery-operated rickshaws in city corporation, municipality, upazila and union parishad areas.
A discussion on the operation of three-wheeled low-speed battery-run rickshaws, commonly known as e-rickshaws, was held at the conference room of the Local Government Ministry at Bangladesh Secretariat here on Thursday.
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam presided over the meeting.
The meeting discussed the measures to effectively manage the battery-run rickshaws in light of urban management, traffic discipline, road safety and existing realities. Representatives of relevant stakeholders also presented various opinions and recommendations.
Mir Shahe Alam said a policy for managing e-rickshaws is being formulated in accordance with the Local Government (City Corporation) Act, 2009 and the Local Government (City Corporation) (Amendment) Act,20 26.
He said effective implementation of the policy would play an important role in controlling traffic congestion, maintaining traffic discipline and ensuring road safety in the cities.
The government authorities would generate revenue for the government exchequer.
The minister further said that, to achieve these objectives, steps would be taken to amend existing regulations and make them time-befitting with a view to establishing a coordinated licensing authority for city corporations, municipalities, upazilas and union councils.
It may be mentioned that relevant provisions and schedules of the Local Government (City Corporation) (Amendment) Act, 2026 have already been amended to create scope for registering battery-operated rickshaws and issuing licenses to their drivers in city corporation areas.
Earlier, on December 14, 2025, the local government division issued the “Rules on the Operation of Three-Wheeled Low-Speed Battery-Operated Rickshaws (E-Rickshaws) in City Corporation areas, 2025” to regulate e-rickshaw operations in city corporation areas. The rules were published in the gazette on December 17, 2025.
At the meeting, Prof Dr Md Hadiuzzaman of the Department of Civil Engineering at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (Burt) provided expert opinions on the issue.
Among others, Dhaka South City Corporation Administrator freedom fighter Md Abdus Salam, Dhaka North City Corporation Administrator Md Shafiqul Islam Khan, Local Government Division Secretary Md Shahidul Hasan, DNCC Chief Executive Officer Muhammad Asaduzzaman, DSCC Chief Executive Officer Md Khaibar Rahman and Additional Commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (Traffic) Md Anisur Rahman attended the meeting.
Senior officials from the ministry and the city corporations concerned were also present.

item.title: Speakers call for action to implement National Urban Policy 2025
item.description:
With more than one-third of Bangladesh’s population living in urban areas and cities contributing nearly 65% of GDP, speakers on Thursday called for coordinated action to implement the National Urban Policy 2025 and translate its commitments into more livable, inclusive and climate-resilient cities.
The call came at the National Dissemination Workshop on National Urban Policy 2025, jointly organized by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Local Government Division (LGD), with support from the UK government, at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre (BCFCC) in Dhaka.
The workshop aimed to disseminate the National Urban Policy 2025 among stakeholders and gather recommendations for drafting its implementation action plan.
The event brought together representatives from government ministries and agencies, local government institutions, development partners, academia, research institutions and the urban development community.
The government approved the country’s first National Urban Policy 2025 as a national framework for more planned, inclusive, sustainable and climate-resilient urban development.
Speaking at the workshop, Md Mahmud Ali, director (additional secretary) of the Urban Development Directorate, said urban development cannot be the responsibility of a single ministry and requires coordination across sectors, with active participation from ministries, public and private institutions, development authorities, academia, professionals and urban residents.
Md Samsul Islam, joint secretary of the Local Government Division, stressed that the next priority is to move from policy to implementation.
“We want the National Urban Policy 2025 to go beyond being a policy document and become an effective tool for real change in urban planning, management, infrastructure development and service delivery,” he said.
Tanvir Mahmud, senior governance specialist at UNDP Bangladesh, said implementation at the local level would ultimately determine the policy’s impact.
“The real success of the National Urban Policy will depend on how effectively it is applied in our cities. National policy directions need to connect with local realities, local capacities and local priorities,” he said.
He added that government ownership should remain at the centre of implementation, while development partners could support the process through technical knowledge, evidence, innovation, capacity development and partnerships.
The National Urban Policy 2025 was developed under the leadership of the Local Government Division, with contributions from an inter-ministerial committee and relevant government institutions, including the Public Works Department, Ministry of Planning, and Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. UNDP provided technical support with assistance from the UK government.
Earlier, Professor Dr Shakil Akther of the Department of Urban and Regional Planning at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology presented the National Urban Policy 2025, followed by an open discussion on its implementation.
Among others, Nathaniel Smith, team leader for climate and environment at the British High Commission; Amit Datta Roy, urban specialist at the Asian Development Bank; Dr Fawzia Farzana, professor at the Department of Urban and Regional Planning at Khulna University; and Yugesh Pradhanang of UNDP spoke at the workshop.

item.title: Madrasa student’s death: Teacher placed on 3-day remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Thursday placed Hafiz Md Zakaria, 35, one of two teachers arrested over the death of a child student at Rowazatul Ulum Hafizia Nurani Madrasa in Rayerbagh’s Jorakhamba area, on a three-day remand.
The court did not hear the remand plea against Hafiz Md Zubayer Ahmed, 20, after his lawyer claimed he was a minor. The court fixed August 18 to hear the matter.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mahbub Alam passed the order on Thursday, said Abdus Sabur, a sub-inspector of the prosecution department.
After the hearing, relatives of the deceased allegedly attacked the accused as police were taking them to jail from the court premises.
The body of Naim Sheikh, 13, was recovered from a bathroom on the third floor of the madrasah around noon on August 3. His mother, Nazma Begum, later filed a case against the two teachers.
Police arrested the two accused from the madrasa around 10:00pm the same day. They were sent to jail the following day.
On August 5, Kadamtali thana Sub-Inspector Amzad Hossain, also the investigating officer in the case, sought five days’ remand for the accused. The court scheduled Thursday for the hearing in their presence.
During Thursday’s hearing, Advocate Harun ur Rashid Khan, appearing for the complainant, argued in favour of granting remand. Zakaria’s lawyer, Emdadul Alam, sought cancellation of the remand plea and bail for his client.
Zubayer’s lawyer claimed that he was a minor, prompting the court to defer the hearing on his remand.
The judge also sought Zakaria’s statement. He told the court that Naim went to the bathroom after the noon prayer call but did not return.
“Even after being called, he did not open the bathroom door. Senior students at the madrasah then opened the door and found him hanging by his shirt sleeve,” Zakaria said.
He said he was in Madanpur at the time and returned to the madrasa after receiving a phone call about the incident.
“When I arrived, his body was still warm. I called a doctor, who came and told us that the child was no longer alive,” he said.
